plates.facing_text:
Chapter Nine: The Corpus
Has No Tongue
The road into Chiapas was a long
argument with the map. The map
supplied a time of arrival. A broken
surface, a stopped truck, and a man
moving three reluctant animals
supplied amendments. Chano
accepted all three without
requesting a revised interface.
Lucía had arranged a visit through
Mateo, a teacher who helped care
for a local archive. The visit had
been planned before the incident at
the wind farm. Bixha remained in
the Isthmus with the lawyer; she
sent updates when there was
something they needed to know. Q
did not ask her to turn the work of
getting two people released into a
continuous feed for his journey.
He sent the Custodian their arrival
contact and expected check-in time.
Then he disabled Castalia's
automatic location updates. That
would not make the rented van
invisible to toll cameras or stop
other people photographing him. It
would prevent one unnecessary
stream of information from leaving
his own device. He told Chano
exactly that, without promising
secrecy.
Children beside the road offered
paper flowers to raise money for a
school event. Q bought one after
asking the price. The girl who
handed it through the window
recognized him and wanted to know
whether he had a battery in his
head. He said it was in his torso.
“Like carrying your lunch,” she
said.
“Much harder to share.”
She gave Chano a flower too. He
had paid for it while Q was
explaining.
Mateo received them in a
blue-painted room behind the
school. On the table stood a radio, a
kettle, and a small storage unit
inside a black metal case. A roof
stain spread above the cupboard. Q
could recognize a maintenance
problem without knowing whether
his hosts wanted a visitor's opinion
of it.
“You were advertised as a
translator,” Mateo said.
“In several languages I'm not
qualified to translate. What work
did you actually ask for?”
“Help reading the terms of a deposit
with Castalia. The Spanish version.”
“I can help identify what it says and
what needs a qualified review. I
can't decide what you should agree
to.”
Mateo took out the agreement.
Beside it lay a passage in Tsotsil. Q

knew the language was represented
in his archive by uneven materials:
dictionaries, publications,
transcripts, and fragments with
uncertain provenance. That was not

pages to improve it.
Mateo would explain the
accompanying passage in Spanish
where necessary. Q left the
translation tool closed.
The agreement promised
preservation and access. Its annex
permitted new forms of reuse
subject to a policy Castalia could
revise. Q marked the
cross-reference and asked whether
the annex had been supplied with
the signature page. Mateo brought
an envelope. It had not.
They spent an hour distinguishing
the copies. Q made a table of
received pages and missing ones for
Mateo to check. When the kettle
began to rattle, Mateo reached past
the agreement to switch it off.
“If we get the other pages, can we
sign?”
“You'll have the whole offer. You
may like it less.”
“I don't like what we have now. The
cupboard leaks.”
Q looked up at the stain. Mateo had
already put a basin beneath its
lowest edge. The promised storage
was not an imaginary benefit,
whatever else the agreement might
take in payment.
“Let's keep the offer open while we
ask them to separate storage from
reuse,” Q said. “And the training
you asked for. I'll put those
questions to the Custodian with
you.”
Mateo drew the signature page back
from the pile Q had marked for
replacement. “Ask. Don't refuse it
for us.”
Q left the page where Mateo had
put it.
On a shelf were poems,
autonomous-assembly minutes,
repair manuals, and a school duty
book. Q asked which were available
for visitors to read. Mateo selected a
published booklet of poems and a
manual whose diagrams had been
corrected in pencil. The minutes
stayed on the shelf.
“I thought you'd choose the poems
first,” Mateo said.
“I was hoping the manual would
explain that noise.”
The radio was giving a low buzz.
Yadira, who worked at the station,
came in and moved its cable away
from the kettle lead. The buzz
diminished. She had heard Q's
question from outside.

“It explains it on page twelve,” she
said.
Q found page twelve. “So it does.”
They showed him the room where
recordings and papers were kept.
There was a shelf list, a digital
register used by two appointed
keepers, and knowledge that had
not yet been entered in either.
Mateo wanted another person
trained to use the register. He did
not want the collection absorbed
into Castalia as the price of
obtaining that help.
Q could review the proposed
transfer inventory without opening
the restricted files. One recorded
item had two accession numbers.
Another was listed as missing
although its box stood on the table.
They resolved the second entry. The
first needed the keeper who was
away that day. Q left it unresolved,
with a question attached, rather
than invent a reason for the
duplication.
Yadira told them why she wanted
the reuse clause examined. A
station she had worked with had
once installed an automatic public
mirror. The supplier had presented
it as permanent memory. An
announcer's live mention of a
caller's route to her mother's house
had then remained searchable after
the caller asked them to remove it.
The woman did not want a former
partner finding her there.
“The station corrected its next
broadcast,” Yadira said. “The host
of the mirror told us only the
project administrator could request
deletion. The project
administrator's address no longer
worked.”
“Did you reach anyone at the host?”
Q asked.
“Eventually. That copy came down.
We never established where else it
went.”
The station had stopped mirroring
everything. It kept scheduled
programs whose speakers had
agreed and used short-lived notes
for notices that needed to expire.
Some records were lost that way.
One of the announcers regretted
losing an interview with his father;
he had assumed somebody had kept
it.
“We wrote a better instruction for
interviews after that,” she said.
“Did people follow it?”
“Some. Would you like me to say
all?”
“Only if we're drafting the funder's
report.”
She laughed, then told him about a
red shoe.

A child had lost it at the market. His
grandmother heard the notice and
brought a bag containing three
shoes she thought might fit. The
announcer tried to ask which one
was the missing shoe. She had not
come to identify the old shoe; she
had come to keep the boy from
walking home barefoot.
“Did one fit?” Q asked.
“Two. Not a pair.”
“A solution likely to be
remembered.”
“He wore them for a week. His
brother said he could tell which foot
was coming around the corner.”
Q asked if he could tell that story to
the Custodian without the child's
name. Yadira said yes, with one
warning: she had not been present
when the grandmother arrived. She
had seen the shoes later. The
splendid conversation with the
announcer was his version of it.
Mateo joined the first part of the
evening call. The Custodian could
arrange a training session without a
transfer, but could not change the
storage offer on his own. Mateo
chose a morning for the session and
asked for a revised offer in writing.
He left Q at the screen when
someone came to fetch the school
duty book.
When Q told the shoe story, he
included Yadira's warning. The
Custodian asked which version
would go in the book.
“Perhaps the one in which we admit
where it came from.”
“Very economical. You'll only need
another paragraph.”
They added the paragraph, then
removed a different one.
“That was a good paragraph,” the
Custodian said.
“It delayed the shoes.”
“It was about narrative time.”
“I know. I had time to notice.”
The Custodian read the shorter
passage aloud. Q waited for the
brother's line, although he knew it
was coming.
Interlude: The Assembly
of Silence
The next morning the station lost
its signal. A roof cable had worked
loose in the wind, and the mains
supply had failed during the night.
The battery could carry only a short
transmission after the repair.
Tomás, the station technician, had
already disconnected the
equipment before anyone asked Q
whether machines were naturally
sympathetic to one another.

Q asked Tomás what would help.
He was given a lamp to hold and a
dry place to stand. His body could
not safely substitute for the station
battery without an adapter they did
not have. Tomás checked the rating
with him, then asked him to bring
the lamp closer.
In the room below, the station's
editorial group was deciding the
bulletin. Three matters could not
wait comfortably: a bridge damaged
by a truck, a twelve-year-old who
had not returned from visiting
relatives, and a meeting about a
proposed repeater on the land
beside the school.
The child's aunt was speaking with
family members by telephone. The
teacher had seen the damaged
railing. The meeting organizers
knew that the company's
representative planned to arrive the
following morning. None possessed
the whole situation, but each
possessed more of one part than Q
did.
“How much time do we have?” he
asked Tomás.
“A few minutes at transmitting
power. I can't promise the voltage
will hold.”
Q brought that limit to the group.
“Can the bridge warning and a
contact for the family fit in one
short bulletin? The meeting notice
might travel by other routes. Who
has already been reached?”
The teacher listed the places where
people might still drive toward the
bridge. Yadira listed the meeting
participants who could be reached
on foot. The aunt said they had not
checked one cousin's house because
nobody there was answering. She
wanted sightings reported to her,
not photographs posted with
guesses about the child.
Q helped shorten the Spanish draft
at her request. The aunt approved
what it said about the child. The
teacher checked the bridge
description: damage to the railing
was observed; safety for vehicles
had not been established. Someone
still needed to warn people at the
turnoff, where a radio bulletin
could not be assumed to reach
them.
The local-language version took
longer. Q waited while its speakers
checked it. He could time it without
claiming to verify its meaning. The
group removed an introduction and
kept the directions. The old man
holding the station key said nobody
needed to hear whom they thanked
before learning where to turn.
Tomás restored the connection.
Yadira read the approved bulletin,
then its second version. The teacher

left with a neighbor to put a
warning at the turnoff. Two other

Q went with one of them, after
confirming that his presence would

“You do make invitations
complicated,” his companion said.
“I used to simplify them. There
have been complaints.”
They delivered six notices. At the
third house, Q was asked to read
the small print on a pump warranty.
Before he reached the exclusions,
the woman who had handed it to
him asked him to lower his voice:
the man who had bought the pump
was still inside. Q moved closer and
finished quietly. At the fourth house
nobody was home; his companion
knew where to leave the notice out
of the rain.
The company representative heard
about the meeting by noon and
wanted a list of those attending.
Yadira gave him the time and the
questions concerning the proposal.
The list was not a condition of his
attendance.
In the afternoon the aunt found the
child at the cousin's house. He had
been asleep after arriving late; the
cousin's phone had no charge. His
aunt had several things to say about
this explanation, none intended for
radio. She asked the station to
announce that the search was over.
Q checked the draft with her. It did
not repeat the child's name. The
station had too little power to
transmit again until a charged
battery arrived, so she approved an
update through the same family
contacts and neighbors already
helping. The later bulletin would
close the notice as well.
“Keep a record that it was
withdrawn,” she told Yadira. “Not
all the story.”
Yadira noted the notice number,
date, and completion. Q crossed out
the last sentence of his journal
entry. It had given him rather a
large part in finding a boy whose
aunt had made the calls. He kept
the account of the bulletin and left
the boy's explanation out.
The technician's cousin brought a
charged battery toward evening. Q
helped carry the old one
downstairs. Before lifting the
replacement, he asked someone to
take the other handle. With one on
either side, they could keep it level
without making his shoulder the
next piece of equipment needing
repair.

The closing bulletin went out. The
bridge still needed inspection. The
repeater meeting would happen in
the morning. It had been a useful
day without becoming a resolved
one.
That evening Yadira showed Q a
report from the organization that
had recorded her brother. The
report had won an award. The
family had received neither the
original recording nor a usable
copy, and the published extract
used three spellings of his name.
Q found the public report from its
title and asked whether she wanted
the file transferred to her device.
She did, but it was the unedited
recording she had come to ask
about.
“The report doesn't give us that,” he
said. “I can help locate the deposit
reference and write to the keeper.
Do you know what your brother
agreed to?”
She had his copy of the release and
authority to handle the request. It
did not authorize the uses described
in the later publicity. Q helped
compare the two documents and
drafted separate requests: restrict
the disputed public extract while it
was reviewed, and supply the
original under the family's recorded
access permission. Yadira checked
the recipient and wording before
sending them. She wanted no post
about the request.
Bixha called with news from the
Isthmus. The detained organizers
had been released, but complaints
and a summons remained. A
consortium brief connected several
people through photographs and
public event records. It cited Q's

them.
He sent the lawyer the corrections
he could substantiate. Deleting his
remaining public pages would not
retrieve that brief, and might
remove material the people
answering it wanted preserved. He
asked which copies the lawyer
needed and kept them out of his
publicity account.
The next morning Mateo invited
him into the archive room again.
Yadira was there with the appointed
keeper and an agreed transport
request. An investigative archive in
Tijuana could receive a sealed
deposit on the Mexican side of the
border. It had accepted the
depositors' limits on access and
publication. Lucía had worked with
one of its members.
“Would you carry this if you go
north?” Mateo asked.

The object was a short cable with a
sealed storage module in its
housing. Calling it a cable had
caused some confusion in the
inventory; the keeper had added
DATA CARRIER underneath. It
contained an encrypted testimony,
according to the deposit record. Q
was not being asked to verify its
contents.
“Why send it with me?”
“You're already in touch with the
receiving group. But if the
complaint makes the trip too risky,
we need to know that before it
leaves.”
They considered waiting, a different
courier, and a remote transfer. The
depositors had declined
transmission through the available
hosted service. The receiving
archive had offered a documented
handover and could retain the
package closed. Q called the named
recipient through the contact Lucía
had used before and confirmed the
arrangement, including what to do
if delivery was interrupted. He did
not ask for decryption keys. They
would remain with the people
entitled to release them.
“I can carry a sealed deposit,” he
said. “I can't guarantee it won't be
searched or seized. My name may
attract exactly that attention.”
The keeper wrote the concern into
the transport record. Mateo
consulted the depositors before
confirming the request. They could
keep the module here while seeking
another carrier if the companions
decided against the trip. Q asked for
an hour before accepting it.
Chano asked to see the route and
expenses before deciding whether
to drive. The journey was
considerably larger than breakfast.
They could fund the first stage and
had a confirmed place to stay at the
other end, but would need to
reassess in the capital. Lucía
wanted to compare the receiving
group's publication records with the
ones she had brought from Mexico
City. She was willing to go north;
she was not willing to spend every
day in the van.
“Nor am I,” Q said. “I want to see
the Pacific. Preferably while we're
stopped.”
Chano moved the phone with its
route between the sugar bowl and
Q's hand. “Put the sea in the
expenses.”
“I understood it was free.”
“Very generous. Does it include a
room?”

shortened the driving stages. The
new total looked less like an

they might enjoy. Chano agreed to
drive as far as the capital, where
they would confirm the remaining
money before committing to the
northern leg. Q took the plan back
to Mateo. Only then did he accept

interruption and make no copy.
They packed the module in a
tamper-evident pouch. The keeper
recorded its identifier and the seal;
Q kept the transport receipt. He had
no ordinary access to the plaintext
and did not connect the module to
his body. The pouch went into the
bag; the local archive's larger black
case stayed on the table.
At a checkpoint later that day, an
officer inspected the van and asked
about the pouch. Q described it as a
sealed data carrier and showed the
receipt.
“What's recorded on it?”
“I'm told it contains testimony for
an archive. I'm carrying it, not
reviewing it. The receipt gives the
deposit contact.”
The officer called a colleague. They
checked the vehicle papers and the
receipt, asked where the handover
would occur, and let them continue
without opening the pouch. No
principle had been established for
the next checkpoint.
Q noted the stop and checked the
seal at their next rest break. Chano
had bought oranges. He put one
beside Q's tablet.
“You can open that,” he said.
“Has the depositor approved the
method?”
“Teeth are traditional. Not
recommended in your case.”
Q used his hands. Juice reached the
corner of the transport receipt,
where Chano's thumb left a small
mark removing any future doubt
that somebody had actually carried
it.
That night Q asked the Custodian to
keep their next writing session
short. They needed to confirm the
northern leg before committing
more money. The Custodian agreed
and asked whether Q still wanted to
make the journey.
“Yes. But I want to reach the person
expecting us more than I want the
border to make a good chapter.”
He saved the plan, set the check-in,
and left the pouch closed.
